mood.summary: Fear is still running high. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq slid into a correction, the worst day since April 2025, on worries that election results will slow AI and data-centre spending. The Fear & Greed index sits in Extreme Fear at 20, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 14 points. Stocks are bouncing on Nov 6 after a strong jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 60,000 expected), but that also firmed bets on a December Fed rate hike.

trending.note: Board as of Sunday 4:05 PM ET; prices are the 2026-11-20 close. Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: Johnson & Johnson
items.about: Johnson & Johnson makes prescription drugs and medical devices, including surgical robots and orthopedic implants.
items.why: Posts say J&J is one of three possible buyers for SELLAS Life Sciences, whose Phase 3 REGAL trial in AML met its overall-survival goal on Nov 17 (41% lower risk of death, median OS 24.0 vs 14.7 months). No deal talks have been confirmed, and several users say the cross-tagging is artificial hype. Shares rose 1.2% Friday to $270.47 as investors moved into defensive pharma during the tech selloff.

items.name: Merck & Co Inc
items.about: Merck develops prescription medicines and vaccines; its best-selling drug is the cancer immunotherapy Keytruda.
items.why: Merck is being tagged alongside SELLAS after its positive Phase 3 AML data on Nov 17. Posts argue that Keytruda's coming patent expiry could push Merck toward oncology deals, but no acquisition talks are confirmed. The stock gained 0.7% Friday to $133.72 after touching $137.17 during the day.

items.name: AbbVie Inc
items.about: AbbVie sells immunology, cancer and neuroscience drugs, including Skyrizi, Rinvoq and the leukemia drug Venclexta.
items.why: Posts name AbbVie as a possible buyer of SELLAS, saying its GPS vaccine could pair with AbbVie's AML drug Venclexta; nothing is confirmed. Shares rose 0.9% Friday to $286.20 as money rotated into large drugmakers during a broad market slide.

items.name: Exxon Mobil Corp
items.about: Exxon Mobil explores for, produces and refines oil and natural gas, and makes chemicals.
items.why: Exxon rose 0.7% to $159.99 Friday as energy held up while tech sold off. Crude is caught between Middle East supply risk and warnings of a global surplus, with WTI near $83–85. Much of the weekend chatter is technical chart calls looking for further weakness from the late-October peak.

items.name: Comcast Corp
items.about: Comcast runs Xfinity broadband and cable, NBCUniversal media and theme parks, and the Peacock streaming service.
items.why: Comcast was little changed (+0.2% to $24.90) in a falling market, and holders are calling it a defensive name. Its latest quarter showed revenue down 6.1% to $29.3 billion while Peacock paid subscribers rose 17% to 48 million, and posts point to a low forward P/E of about 7.

items.name: YieldMax Semiconductor Portfolio Option Income ETF
items.about: CHPY is a YieldMax ETF that holds semiconductor stocks and sells options on them to pay large monthly distributions.
items.why: The fund fell 10.0% Friday to $43.82 as semiconductor stocks were hit in the AI-led selloff that pushed the Nasdaq into correction. Posts debate whether its roughly 41% distribution rate can hold up, and note the price is down about 40% over six months.

items.name: Walt Disney Co
items.about: Disney runs theme parks and cruises, film studios, ESPN and the Disney+ and Hulu streaming services.
items.why: Disney beat on Nov 17 with adjusted EPS of $1.77 versus about $1.68 expected and recently hit a 52-week high on strong parks demand. It slipped 1.9% Friday to $117.98 with the broad market, and options are pricing a move of about 3.3% this holiday-shortened week.

items.name: RTX Corporation
items.about: RTX makes Pratt & Whitney jet engines, Collins aerospace systems and Raytheon missiles and defense electronics.
items.why: RTX picked up new missile contracts this week, and posts cite a fiscal 2027 request that nearly doubles missile-defense spending and a record $340 billion backlog. The stock still fell 1.3% Friday to $190.17 in the broad selloff.

items.name: GE Aerospace
items.about: GE Aerospace designs, builds and services jet engines for commercial airlines and the military.
items.why: GE fell 2.9% Friday to $309.62 with the market, even after a White House summary listed a $12 billion Boeing and GE Aerospace sale to the Philippines. Its last quarter showed revenue up 15.9% to $14.1 billion and orders up 49% to $19.0 billion.

items.name: ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil
items.about: UCO is a ProShares ETF that aims to return twice the daily move of crude oil futures.
items.why: UCO rose 0.6% Friday to $49.19 as WTI crude climbed back toward $85 ahead of Thanksgiving. Oil is being pulled between Middle East risk (Iran says talks with the U.S. continue through mediators, while Trump says no acceptable deal is on offer) and record U.S. output.

items.name: Mastercard Inc
items.about: Mastercard runs a global card-payments network that connects shoppers, merchants and banks.
items.why: Trump said Saturday he would work with the incoming Democratic Congress to cap credit card interest rates at 10%, and that headline is circulating on the stream. A $167.5 million Visa/Mastercard ATM-fee settlement is also open for claims. Shares eased 0.1% Friday to $625.59.

items.name: YieldMax MSTR Option Income Strategy ETF
items.about: MSTY is a YieldMax ETF that sells options on Strategy (MSTR) shares to pay large monthly distributions.
items.why: MSTY fell 9.7% Friday to $7.61 after bitcoin dropped below $60,000 for the first time since July and Strategy hit a 52-week low. Its Nov 18 distribution of $0.1206 a share was about 95% return of capital, and posts point out that a high payout rate does not mean a positive total return.

items.name: Amgen Inc
items.about: Amgen is a biotech company selling drugs for cholesterol, bone health, inflammation and cancer.
items.why: Piper Sandler raised its Amgen target to $542 from $457, citing a Sjögren's disease candidate and the lung cancer drug Imdelltra. Last quarter's revenue rose 8.5% to $10.4 billion, with Repatha sales up 37%. Shares slipped 0.2% Friday to $435.64.

items.name: Global X Dow 30 Covered Call ETF
items.about: DJIA is a Global X ETF that holds the 30 Dow stocks and sells call options on the index for income.
items.why: Investors are using it to talk about the overall market after a brutal week: the S&P 500 fell 3.7% and closed below 7,000, the Dow lost 1.9%, and the Nasdaq had its worst week in years. The fund fell 1.9% Friday to $21.00.

items.name: Snowflake Inc
items.about: Snowflake sells a cloud data platform that companies pay for based on how much computing they use.
items.why: Snowflake fell 5.1% Friday to $254.82 as AI-linked software sold off. Bears argue that usage-based revenue is exposed if companies cut AI test projects, and posts cite a BofA survey in which only 16% of fund managers want more capex.

items.name: Morgan Stanley
items.about: Morgan Stanley is an investment bank and wealth manager that advises on deals, trades securities and manages client money.
items.why: Morgan Stanley fell 5.3% Friday to $165.67, now 29% below its 52-week high, as bank stocks dropped. Posts also discuss its role in Anthropic's IPO, saying the underwriters used the over-allotment option within a day, and note heavy trading in January $165 puts.

items.name: Delta Air Lines, Inc.
items.about: Delta Air Lines is a major U.S. airline with its main hub in Atlanta.
items.why: Delta's automated weight-and-balance system failed on Sunday morning, Nov 22. The FAA briefly halted Atlanta-bound Delta flights, and hundreds to thousands of flights were delayed as crews used manual workarounds just before Thanksgiving. The stock had already fallen 3.8% Friday to $80.01.

items.name: Citigroup Inc
items.about: Citigroup is a global bank serving corporations, institutions and consumers in about 160 countries.
items.why: Citi fell 4.0% Friday to $110.62 and is down about 11.6% over five days. Reports cited in posts say a UK or European trading unit understated risk-weighted assets by about $35 billion after trades were booked incorrectly, which led to a capital injection into the subsidiary. Posts also note large put buying.

items.name: Freeport-McMoRan Inc
items.about: Freeport-McMoRan mines copper, gold and molybdenum, with large mines in Indonesia and the Americas.
items.why: Freeport fell 6.4% Friday to $45.99 as copper, gold and silver plunged and trend-following funds added to short positions. Mining.com reports that Paul Tudor Jones cut his FCX stake by nearly 90%. Posts are split between dip buyers and people warning of further losses.

items.name: Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF
items.about: MAGS is a Roundhill ETF that holds equal stakes in the seven mega-cap tech stocks: Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Tesla.
items.why: MAGS fell 5.2% Friday to $61.66 and is about 17% below its high, as worries about AI valuations hit mega-cap tech hardest during the Nasdaq's worst week in years. Sentiment on the stream is mostly bearish, with many posts warning that a bounce may not last.
